questions.q: Why did Hannah laugh at her enemies?
questions.a: Hannah laughed because she rejoiced in Yahweh’s salvation.

questions.q: Why does Hannah say that people should not boast or speak arrogantly?
questions.a: People should not boast or speak arrogantly because Yahweh is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.

questions.q: In Hannah’s song, who is the one who is unable to have more children?
questions.a: The woman who had many children before is not able to have any more.

questions.q: Who decides death and life, or who goes down to Sheol or is raised up?
questions.a: Yahweh is the one who decides death and life, and who causes people to go down to Sheol or to come up from there.

questions.q: Who makes people poor or rich?
questions.a: Yahweh makes people poor, and he makes them rich.

questions.q: Who raises up the poor and lifts the needy to sit in a seat of honor?
questions.a: Yahweh raises them up to sit in a seat of honor.

questions.q: Who does Hannah say will protect the feet of his faithful people and silence the wicked in darkness?
questions.a: Hannah says that Yahweh will guard the feet of his faithful people and will silence the wicked.

questions.q: Who will judge the ends of the earth and give strength to his king?
questions.a: Yahweh will judge the ends of the earth and give strength to his king.

questions.q: What child served Yahweh in the presence of Eli the priest?
questions.a: Samuel served Yahweh in the presence of Eli the priest.

questions.q: Whose sons were wicked men who did not know Yahweh?
questions.a: Eli the priest’s sons did very bad things.

questions.q: What was the custom of the priests with the people at the time of sacrifice?
questions.a: The custom was for the priest’s servant to come with a three-pronged fork while the meat was boiling and take whatever the fork brought up for the priest.

questions.q: What evil thing did Eli’s sons have their servant do?
questions.a: They had their servant demand raw meat for the priest before the fat was burned as an offering to Yahweh, and had him take it by force if the person refused.

questions.q: Why was the sin of Eli’s sons so great?
questions.a: Their sin was great before Yahweh because the men were treating very disrespectfully the offerings that people were bringing to Yahweh.

questions.q: What would Samuel’s mother make for him from year to year to clothe him?
questions.a: She would make him a small robe each year.

questions.q: How would Eli bless Elkanah and his wife?
questions.a: Eli blessed them by asking Yahweh to give them more children from Hannah.

questions.q: What was Yahweh’s response to Eli’s prayer for Samuel’s parents to have more children?
questions.a: Yahweh helped Hannah, and she bore three more sons and two daughters.

questions.q: What did Eli say to his sons when he heard evil reports about them?
questions.a: Eli told his sons that the report he was hearing from Yahweh’s people about their evil deeds was not good. He told them to stop doing what they were doing.

questions.q: Why did Eli’s sons not listen to his voice?
questions.a: Eli’s sons did not listen to his voice because Yahweh desired to make them die.

questions.q: Who grew up and was good in the sight of Yahweh and also with men?
questions.a: Samuel grew up and was good in the sight of Yahweh and with men.

questions.q: Who told Eli that Yahweh chose Eli’s ancestors out of all the tribes of Israel to be Yahweh’s priest?
questions.a: A man of God told Eli that Yahweh had chosen his ancestors.

questions.q: How had Eli and his sons scorned Yahweh’s sacrifices and offerings?
questions.a: They scorned the sacrifices and offerings by honoring his sons above Yahweh and fattening themselves on the best parts of offerings.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Eli would happen to the men in his family?
questions.a: Yahweh told Eli that all the men born in his family would die young.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would be a sign to Eli that his prophecy would come true?
questions.a: The sign would be that both of his sons would die on the same day.

questions.q: Who will walk before Yahweh’s faithful priest always?
questions.a: Yahweh has chosen another man who will serve him faithfully and continually be a helper to the king whom Yahweh will appoint.

questions.q: Why will everyone left in Eli’s family come and bow down to the faithful priest?
questions.a: They will ask him to allow them to work with the other priests so that they can have food to eat.

commentary.text: The wickedness of Eli's sons, Samuel's ministry.

Verses 1–10 Hannah's heart rejoiced, not in Samuel, but in the Lord. She looks beyond the gift, and praises the Giver. She rejoiced in the salvation of the Lord, and in expectation of His coming, who is the whole salvation of his people. The strong are soon weakened, and the weak are soon strengthened, when God pleases. Are we poor? God made us poor, which is a good reason why we should be content, and make up our minds to our condition. Are we rich? God made us rich, which is a good reason why we should be thankful, and serve him cheerfully, and do good with the abundance he gives us. He respects not man's wisdom or fancied excellences, but chooses those whom the world accounts foolish, teaching them to feel their guilt, and to value his free and precious salvation. This prophecy looks to the kingdom of Christ, that kingdom of grace, of which Hannah speaks, after having spoken largely of the kingdom of providence. And here is the first time that we meet with the name MESSIAH, or his Anointed. The subjects of Christ's kingdom will be safe, and the enemies of it will be ruined; for the Anointed, the Lord Christ, is able to save, and to destroy.

Samuel, being devoted to the Lord in a special manner, was from a child employed about the sanctuary in the services he was capable of. As he did this with a pious disposition of mind, it was called ministering unto the Lord. He received a blessing from the Lord. Those young people who serve God as well as they can, he will enable to improve, that they may serve him better. Eli shunned trouble and exertion. This led him to indulge his children, without using parental authority to restrain and correct them when young. He winked at the abuses in the service of the sanctuary till they became customs, and led to abominations; and his sons, who should have taught those that engaged in the service of the sanctuary what was good, solicited them to wickedness. Their offence was committed even in offering the sacrifices for sins, which typified the atonement of the Saviour! Sins against the remedy, the atonement itself, are most dangerous, they tread under foot the blood of the covenant. Eli's reproof was far too mild and gentle. In general, none are more abandoned than the degenerate children of godly persons, when they break through restraints.

Those who allow their children in any evil way, and do not use their authority to restrain and punish them, in effect honour them more than God. Let Eli's example excite parents earnestly to strive against the beginnings of wickedness, and to train up their children in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. In the midst of the sentence against the house of Eli, mercy is promised to Israel. God's work shall never fall to the ground for want of hands to carry it on. Christ is that merciful and faithful High Priest, whom God raised up when the Levitical priesthood was thrown off, who in all things did his Father's mind, and for whom God will build a sure house, build it on a rock, so that hell cannot prevail against it.
